source: Owner 18 Nov 2026: "make a list of smaller bug fixes for Apex to work on ... teach apex how to spot the bugs and fix them"
steps: Reproduce first: run the failing test with run_tests, or find the error in the log or traceback the task quotes. Write down the exact error line and file:line before changing anything.

Read the code at that line with read_file (20-40 lines around it) and grep_repo for the function or name involved. Find the cause, not just the place it surfaced (e.g. a missing import, a write in a read-only request, a wrong key).
Check history: grep the Studio/KC records (knowledge_search 'Practice <n>' or the file name) - the code was usually changed for a reason; do not undo an owner's earlier fix.

Decide which side is out of date: the code or the test. Backlog sweep 20 Nov 2026: 6 of 8 stuck bugs were stale tests - a renamed file (watchdog_deos -> watchdog_does), an owner rule the test predates (Fred only takes over planned steps), a stub missing a field the real endpoint returns (ok: true), a deliberate newer answer (ALREADY APPLIED), or this machine's state (model files that left the repo, a changed IP). When the code changed on purpose (a Practice, an owner note, git log), update the test to the deliberate behaviour or make it independent of this machine (stand-in files, monkeypatch), and say so in the report - that is not weakening a test. Change the code only when it is the code that is wrong.
Write a test that fails now and will pass after the fix (tests/test_bug_<short_name>.py), small and self-contained (sqlite3 ':memory:', monkeypatch; no network, no real model).
Make the smallest change that fixes the cause with propose_patch (exact old text, new text). One cause per patch; no unrelated clean-up.
Run the new test AND the existing tests of the files you touched with run_tests. If anything fails, read the output and fix it - never weaken a test to make it pass.
Report in 3-5 lines: the error, the cause (file:line), the fix, the tests that passed (alm_run_id). If you could not reproduce the bug, say so and stop - do not guess a fix.
